parameters.content:
## 1 · Ingestion

**Schedule** fires 16:30 on weekdays. The arXiv RSS feed is rebuilt around 04:00 UTC, so anything after that sees a complete batch; the hour is simply when you want to read it. The Manual Trigger beside it exists so the pipeline can be replayed without waiting a day.

**Config** is the only node anyone should need to edit. Everything downstream reads it through `$('Config')`, so thresholds, category lists and the reader profile are never buried inside another node. The Discord webhook URL and the chat ID come from `$env`, which is why this export carries no secrets.

**Fetch → Parse → Normalise** turns the RSS feed into one clean item per paper. The source is `rss.arxiv.org`, not the query API: a separate service with separate rate limits, which matters on n8n Cloud where the outbound IP is shared with every other tenant.

**New and Cross-Lists Only** drops `replace` announcements — revisions of papers announced earlier, and close to half of a typical feed. The RSS source exposes this; the query API did not, which is the other reason to prefer it.

**Cap Papers Per Run** takes the newest `max_papers_per_run` — the free-tier budget, in papers. It sits **before** the deduplicator on purpose: everything the deduplicator sees is recorded as seen, so capping after it would mark 40 papers read that were never analysed, and they would never come back.

**Unseen Papers Only** is cross-execution deduplication keyed on the arXiv ID. Cross-listed papers reappear in the feed for days; this is what stops the same paper being summarised, and paid for, twice.

## 1b · First-stage ranking

A day across five categories is around 900 announcements. The run can afford ten model calls, so something has to choose which ten.

**Rank via Service** sends every candidate to the local bi-encoder in `ranker/` and gets them back ordered by similarity to the reader profile. No batch ceiling, no API quota, no cost - and it stores each paper with the vector it just computed, which is what the clustering and the near-duplicate search need later.

This replaced an embeddings API whose request cap is 100 texts: 40 went to the profile’s own concepts, 60 papers got ranked and 862 were dropped unranked. Nothing said so - the fallback did its job and the digest looked fine.

**It degrades gracefully, and says when it does.** On failure the papers keep the feed order and `ranked_by` is stamped `recency`, which travels as far as the Telegram message.

## 2 · Analysis — one paper at a time

**Loop Over Papers** runs with a batch size of 1. A failure on paper 34 then costs one model call rather than the whole batch, and the loop resumes where it stopped.

**Throttle** is the second half of staying inside the free tier. Gemini's free plan caps requests *per minute*; eight seconds per iteration holds the pipeline at 7.5/min, comfortably under a 10/min ceiling. At the default cap of 10 papers the loop spends about 80 seconds waiting, unattended, at 07:30. Set `llm_throttle_seconds` to 0 on a paid key.

**Analyse Paper** is a Basic LLM Chain with a **structured output parser** attached. The schema guarantees *shapes* — an array stays an array — while every value constraint is enforced downstream in `Merge Analysis`, because Gemini ignores half of JSON Schema but the parser still validates against it.

Three retries (n8n caps the spacing at 5s, which is why the **Throttle** in front matters more than the retry here), then the **error output** sends the paper to `Skipped`. One abstract the model cannot parse must not cost the rest of the run.

The system prompt carries the reader profile and a controlled tag vocabulary. Scoring rules spell out what a 3 and a 9 mean, because "rate this 0-10" without anchors drifts upward every run.

**Relevant Enough?** is an IF, not a Filter. Both branches feed back into the loop, so a rejected paper still closes its iteration. A Filter would drop the item and the loop would stall.

## 5 · Memory

The same `done` output also goes to the store: every paper the run touched, kept **and** rejected.

The rejects are the point. The store exists to answer *was the cheap ranker right?*, and that needs both halves of the decision.

Optional throughout. An empty `store_url` costs the memory, never the digest.

## 3 · Discord — the archive

One rich embed per paper in `#ai-papers`, colour-coded by score. The channel becomes the searchable archive; Discord's own search covers it.

**Build Paper Embed** enforces Discord's limits before the request leaves n8n — title 256, description 4096, field value 1024, and 6000 characters across the *whole* embed. Blow any one of them and the API returns a 400 with no usable error body, which is a miserable thing to debug at 07:31.

It also sets `allowed_mentions: { parse: [] }`. arXiv titles are not a trusted input: one containing `@everyone` would otherwise ping the whole server.

**Posted with an HTTP Request node**, not the Discord node. A webhook is a plain POST with a JSON body — no auth header, no SDK — and the payload has to be built in code anyway, because the Discord node's embed UI is a fixed collection that cannot express a variable number of fields. The URL is a secret and comes from `$env`, so it never lands in this export.

A webhook means no bot: no application, no token, no gateway, no server permissions. The trade is that threads and reactions need Bot auth.

**Collect Result** puts the paper back on the item — the Discord response replaces it — so the digest branch still has something to rank.

## 4 · Telegram — the daily nudge

Reached through the loop's **done** output, so it runs exactly once, after every paper has been filed.

Selecting, ranking and capping at `digest_size` all happen inside the Code node. A Filter/Sort/Limit chain reads better on a canvas but cannot render a day when nothing clears the bar - n8n skips a node with zero input items, so the message would simply never be sent, and silence is indistinguishable from a crash.

**Build Telegram Digest** escapes HTML — an unescaped `<` in a paper title returns a 400 from the Bot API — and packs entries into ≤3500-character chunks on paper boundaries, because Telegram hard-fails at 4096.

nodes.notes: The RSS feed is rebuilt around 04:00 UTC each weekday, so any run after that sees a complete batch. The exact hour is a matter of when you want to read it.

assignments.name: research_profile
assignments.value:
Applied ML engineer and MSc researcher. Ships production systems and reads papers for things that can be implemented this month.

Actively working on: mechanistic interpretability of transformers, attention head analysis, head specialisation metrics, probing what BERT and GPT-2 class models encode, visualising attention, inspecting model internals.

Also working on: retrieval-augmented generation that stays grounded and cites its sources, structured LLM output, schema-constrained decoding, natural language to validated query interfaces, evaluation of LLM systems.

Also working on: explainability for tabular models, SHAP and feature attribution, embedding-based similarity search over structured data, football analytics from event data, player similarity and role classification.

Interested in: small open-weight models that run locally, Gemma and Qwen and Llama class models, quantisation, efficient inference on CPU, compact embedding models, measuring bias in language models, fairness evaluation of language models, honest benchmarks with reproducible code.

Not interested in: large-scale pretraining, scaling laws for frontier models, incremental leaderboard deltas, pure theory with no implementation, hardware accelerator papers, kernel level systems work, reinforcement learning for games, robotics, image generation, video generation.

nodes.name: Config
nodes.notes: Single source of truth. Tune the pipeline here, nowhere else.

nodes.name: Fetch arXiv Feed
nodes.notes: The RSS host, not export.arxiv.org/api/query - separate service, separate rate limits, which matters on shared Cloud IPs. Still identify yourself, and pin this output while iterating rather than re-fetching.

nodes.name: New and Cross-Lists Only
nodes.notes: Drops announce_type replace AND replace-cross - both are revisions of papers announced earlier, and together they are ~45% of a typical feed. notStartsWith rather than notEquals because replace-cross exists and an equality test silently lets it through.

nodes.name: Rank via Service
nodes.notes: Local bi-encoder, no batch ceiling and no API quota. 120s because a cold start loads the model. On failure the run continues on chronological order.

nodes.name: Cap Papers Per Run
nodes.notes: Placed BEFORE the deduplicator on purpose: papers past the cap are never marked seen, so raising the cap later does not leave a permanent hole.

nodes.name: Unseen Papers Only
nodes.notes: Keyed on arXiv ID, persisted across executions.

nodes.name: Throttle (free tier)
nodes.notes: Paces the loop under the Gemini free-tier requests-per-minute cap.

messageValues.message:
=You are a research analyst who triages the daily arXiv firehose for one specific reader. You see one paper at a time and you only ever see its abstract — never the full text.

READER PROFILE
{{ $('Config').first().json.research_profile }}

CONTROLLED VOCABULARY (prefer these tags, in this exact spelling)
{{ $('Config').first().json.topic_vocabulary }}

HOW TO SCORE
relevance_score is about *this reader*, not about the paper's importance to the field.
  9-10  Directly actionable for the reader's current work. They would open the PDF today.
  7-8   Clearly inside their interests; worth a read this week.
  5-6   Adjacent. Useful context, no urgency.
  3-4   Same broad field, wrong sub-area.
  0-2   Unrelated, or a marginal increment on a topic they do not track.
Do not inflate. A normal day should produce a handful of papers at 7+, not twenty.

HARD RULES
- Ground every claim in the abstract. If a number, dataset or baseline is not stated there, do not state it.
- When the abstract makes no empirical claim, write "Not stated in the abstract." rather than guessing.
- Do not praise the paper. No "novel", "groundbreaking", "significant advance" unless the abstract's own numbers justify it, and then cite the number instead of the adjective.
- Assume the reader knows ML fundamentals. Never define transformer, attention, fine-tuning, RAG, etc.
- topics: 2 to 5 tags, lowercase, hyphenated. Reuse the controlled vocabulary; invent at most one new tag, and only when nothing in the list fits.
- relevance_score is a whole number from 0 to 10. Not a string, not "8/10", not 8.5.
- paper_type is exactly one of: method, benchmark, dataset, theory, survey, application, position.
- reading_priority is exactly one of: read-now, read-this-week, skim, archive.
- key_contributions holds 1 to 4 entries. Every field is required; when you have nothing to say, write "Not stated in the abstract." rather than omitting the key or returning null.
- Return one JSON object and nothing else. No markdown code fences, no commentary before or after it.
- Write in {{ $('Config').first().json.digest_language }}.

nodes.name: Analyse Paper
nodes.notes: Three tries, 5s apart - n8n caps retry spacing at 5s, so the real defence against a 429 is the Throttle node in front, not this. After the retries the paper is skipped rather than failing the whole run.

nodes.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
nodes.notes: 8192 output tokens. 2.5 Flash is a thinking model and its reasoning is billed against this same budget - a limit sized for the visible answer alone gets spent on thinking and truncates the JSON mid-string.

nodes.name: Build Paper Embed
nodes.notes: Enforces every Discord embed limit before the request is made.

nodes.name: Discord - Post Paper Card
nodes.notes: A Discord webhook is a plain POST with a JSON body - no auth header, no SDK. The payload is built in the previous node because the Discord node's embed UI is a fixed collection and cannot express a variable number of fields.

nodes.name: Skipped
nodes.notes: Low score, or analysis failed. Either way the iteration has to close or the loop stalls.

nodes.name: Record in Store
nodes.notes: Optional. Empty store_url, or a store that is down, costs the memory - never the digest.

nodes.name: Build Telegram Digest
nodes.notes: Selects, ranks and caps in code. A Filter/Sort/Limit chain cannot render a quiet day: n8n skips a node with no input items, so the digest would never be sent.
